summary: All existing identities screened against every PDF page with names, aliases and separately qualified surname variants; targeted body-text rereading adds source accounts and relationships absent from the profile-based audit. Editorial additions, generic terms, relative-name collisions and inferred ownership were excluded.

coverage.limits: Candidate screening covers all supplied pages and all current identity inventories. Body passages or contextual excerpts on the listed pages were reviewed manually, not every sentence of every page. Common surnames, OCR failures and every passing reference are not claimed to be exhaustively resolved; this is not a complete transcription of every relationship in the book. Later generated short-form/acronym leads expand the search inventory; their candidate inventories were screened, with selected contexts reread and acronym collisions recorded. Remaining individual passages are not counted as completed manual review.

eventUpdates.description: Quigley names Willard and Dorothy Straight as the founders of The New Republic in 1914, financed with Dorothy’s Whitney inheritance, and describes Walter Lippmann’s early editorial direction.

sourceSummary.summary: Quigley names Willard and Dorothy Straight as the founders of The New Republic in 1914, financed with Dorothy’s Whitney inheritance, and describes Walter Lippmann’s early editorial direction.
details: The later body passage supplies the identities missing from the early financing overview: Willard was a Morgan partner and former assistant to Robert Hart; Dorothy financed the magazine. Quigley separately describes Lippmann’s role in giving the publication an Anglophile direction. These roles are not interchangeable.

Quigley interprets the magazine as a meeting point between reform publishing and financial influence. His argument about motives is attributed to him, and the founding does not prove all contributors shared a single policy or belonged to the same network. Later editorial control by their son Michael is a separate development.
sourceSummary.context: Connects the founders’ individual timelines with publishing, Whitney-family financing and the Morgan network, while separating named roles from the author’s political interpretation.
sourceSummary.precisionNote: The source supplies the foundation year, 1914. January 1 is only the timeline coordinate, not an asserted founding day.
